title: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude
gist: Anthropic reports early, mostly preclinical results from six drug-development partnerships and its own programs: a 70%-shorter CAR T design with ~10x receptor expression, ~35,000 antibody designs in a month, 89% less manufacturing-document review time at Enveda, and a one-person muscular dystrophy program reaching mouse data in under 18 months. It frames the bottleneck as distributed across the whole pipeline and plans to scale up, with human trials for its own candidate possibly starting late 2028.

insights.claim: Anthropic's life sciences strategy rests on the view that drug development has no single bottleneck: constraints are spread across target identification, molecule design, manufacturing, regulatory filings and trial design, so AI must be embedded across all of them rather than only in molecule generation.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Value capture in AI-for-drug-development may accrue to workflow integrators, not just molecule-design specialists; watch for horizontal deployments.
insights.quote: There is no single problem to solve; the bottlenecks are distributed all throughout the drug development process.
insights.locator: Our strategy to realize AI’s medical benefits

insights.claim: Anthropic is partnering with six drug developers (BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines, The Column Group) and running its own programs, explicitly to learn model limitations, build case studies and generate direct drug impact; it says it has already prioritized model improvements from these learnings and plans to scale up substantially.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Signals a sustained frontier-lab push into pharma; expect more biotech and pharma partnership announcements and a model roadmap tuned to biology.
insights.locator: This work serves our goals in three ways

insights.claim: All of the reported work is early and mostly preclinical, so none of the claimed gains has yet been tested in humans; Anthropic says it plans to extend into clinical-stage programs as partners advance.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Discount the headline efficiency numbers until clinical readouts exist; the real test of value is human trial success rates.
insights.quote: All of this research is still at an early stage.
insights.locator: Extending our work in the life sciences

insights.claim: At Generate Biomedicines, six scientists using Claude Code proposed a CAR T design about 70% shorter than the standard version that, in lab tests, let immune cells make roughly 10 times as many receptors, killed tumor cells more efficiently and stayed active longer, which could free genetic space to target solid tumors.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: If the shortened design generalizes, it supports CAR T expansion into solid tumors, a large unmet market; lab results only so far.

insights.claim: For Divergence Labs' food-allergy approach of detaching IgE from immune cells, Claude largely autonomously generated roughly 35,000 antibody designs in about a month, yielding three IgE binders and 20 IgE-dislodgers, three of which appeared to dislodge IgE more than the standard medication.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Shows AI can run the high-volume hit-generation stage at scale; the combined two-arm drug is still unbuilt, so efficacy remains unproven.

insights.claim: At BigHat Biosciences, Claude connected to the lab data system Reccy proposed changes to two antibody-fragment leads and about 1,010 variants were made and tested in about 10 weeks; the best versions bound more than 10x more tightly, one stayed in solution 18°C higher and another clumped more than 100x more slowly.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: AI paired with an automated lab shortens design-make-test loops; lead-optimization cycle time is a metric to track across AI-biotech peers.

insights.claim: Mid-project, Claude and an Anthropic researcher reanalyzed BigHat's raw data, concluded the standard heat-stability and clumping metrics were misleading, and proposed alternative metrics and a protocol change whose main predictions then held, an example of AI questioning the measurement rather than just optimizing it.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Suggests value from AI critiquing assay design, not only executing it; a differentiator versus pure generative-design tools.
insights.quote: the team suspected the standard heat-stability and clumping metrics were misleading

insights.claim: At Enveda, manufacturing chemists spent up to 75% of their time on paperwork; a Claude-based system reviewing 1,061 pages caught all 11 issues human reviewers had found plus seven they missed, cutting review time by 89%, from over 25 hours to under three.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Documentation and quality review is a concrete, near-term place where AI removes cost from clinical-stage companies, which could lower burn per program.
insights.quote: manufacturing chemists spent up to 75% of their time on paperwork

insights.claim: Claude wrote the first draft of an important regulatory document at Enveda in four hours versus about three months by hand, and for a second document Enveda's standard human review found only one minor error.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Regulatory-writing speedups could compress time to IND-type filings; regulator acceptance of AI-drafted submissions is the thing to monitor.

insights.claim: Bristol Myers Squibb is using Claude to assess an early-stage drug's clinical trial plans and estimate the likelihood of trial success, with plans to expand in 2027 to test whether this raises the probability of success in early development; BMS says a single prompt produced an analysis that would otherwise take days.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: A large pharma adopting AI for portfolio-level decisions could shift capital allocation in R&D; 2027 results are a checkpoint.
insights.quote: From a single prompt, Claude generated a robust initial analysis that helped inform our assessment of different development options, which would otherwise take days to complete.

insights.claim: Anthropic argues biotech investors favor safer, previously validated ideas because drug discovery is slow, expensive and failure-prone, and that cutting time and cost with AI could let investors back riskier, higher-impact ideas.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: If AI lowers the cost of a failed program, the funding mix could tilt toward novel targets; watch venture allocation in biotech.
insights.quote: investors in biotechnology companies have favored safer, previously validated ideas over riskier new ones

insights.claim: The Column Group is establishing Pleiades, a new company that will use Claude to run many more and more complex drug programs than a small team normally could; its first Claude skill, for assessing whether drug targets are worth pursuing, has been evaluated on 45 target-disease pairs.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Pleiades is a live test of an AI-native, low-headcount biotech model; if it works the article says it could be replicated across the industry.

insights.claim: Anthropic acquired Mithril Medicine, a one-person company whose founder used Claude to organize contracts, logistics and experiments with 11 external labs, taking a possible muscular dystrophy treatment from idea to promising mouse results in under 18 months; Anthropic expects a drug could start human trials as soon as late 2028 if candidates hold up.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: A one-person drug program reaching animal data suggests AI can substitute for operational headcount; the late-2028 clinical-start date is a milestone to track.
insights.quote: Mithril took a possible treatment for one form of muscular dystrophy from an idea to promising results in mice in less than 18 months

insights.claim: Anthropic is broadening access through Claude Science, an AI workbench for researchers, credits for life scientists, a call for guest investigators, and a Life Sciences Verification Program giving trusted organizations its most powerful models with more permissive safeguards, acknowledging that misuse-prevention safeguards can impede legitimate biological research.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Tiered access to biology-capable models is a template for dual-use governance and a go-to-market channel into pharma and biotech.
insights.quote: safeguards, which are necessary to prevent misuse but which can impede legitimate biological research
insights.locator: Extending our work in the life sciences
